source.title: SAE-FD: Sparse Autoencoder Feature Distillation for Continual Learning of Large Language Models
source.authors: Ming-Xu Zhang; Yu-Han Li; Lu-Jun Li; Da-Zhong Shen; Hui Xiong; Ying Sun

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how well sparse autoencoders reconstruct LLM activations, including after continual fine-tuning. These results bear on SAE feature recoverability and fidelity, but it does not test the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The study cites the superposition hypothesis as theoretical motivation and uses SAE features for continual learning. The continual-learning benchmark scores and comparisons among learning methods are not rows because they measure the method's task performance, not superposition or feature geometry. The SAE reconstruction measurements are included.
record.test_reason: The study is a continual-learning method paper (SAE-FD) that uses Gated SAEs as a tool. It cites superposition only as motivation. Its SAE measurements are sanity checks of the tool: variance explained on held-out data, and frozen-SAE reconstruction fidelity after LoRA fine-tuning. No sparsity level (L0), feature interpretability, neuron spread, dictionary stability or canonicality is measured, so no result bears on whether any version holds. Everything else reported is the method's task performance (AA/BWT) against baselines.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors' main conclusion is that SAE-FD, by regularizing in sparse SAE feature space, outperforms dense-space continual-learning methods across three 7B models. The frozen-SAE fidelity result is a secondary justification in an appendix.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and applies Gated SAEs for continual-learning regularization and measures reconstruction fidelity; it does not reproduce the original toy-network method or its feature-geometry experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction variance explained decreases over successive TRACE tasks for the frozen Vicuna-7B SAE.

fits_no_version.finding: A frozen Gated SAE on Vicuna-7B final-layer MLP activations keeps above 90% variance explained and cosine above 0.96 across 8 LoRA fine-tuning tasks. Variance explained is 94.65% at base, below the >99% held-out value, which the authors attribute to a domain gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction fidelity is robust to moderate distribution shift and LoRA fine-tuning of the underlying model.

fits_no_version.finding: Distillation in SAE feature space beats raw-activation MSE distillation for continual learning. On Vicuna, AA is 53.50 vs 51.31. On Mistral, BWT is −1.47 vs −3.33 (Table 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature space is a more effective regularization target than dense activations (a method-utility claim, not a superposition claim).

record.problems: The reconstruction-stability evaluation is reported for Vicuna-7B with 500 random samples per evaluation; no uncertainty estimates are given. The measurements do not establish whether features are canonical or semantically complete.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant result rows omitted. Continual-learning task accuracy, backward transfer, method ablations, and baseline comparisons are excluded because they do not directly measure the claim's feature-representation properties.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or feature importance.
No analysis of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
No measure of features spread across neurons, SAE sparsity or interpretability, and no comparison with other dictionaries. Only reconstruction fidelity is reported.
No test of completeness, cross-seed stability or canonicality of SAE features.
No comparison of 1-D and multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its supports labels for V4 and V5 are not warranted. The SAE metrics validate the tool and do not test superposition or the status of dictionary features. Only one layer (final MLP, last token) is used. No uncertainty is reported, and the fidelity analysis covers only Vicuna-7B with 500 samples.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep, transition, or regular geometry are tested.
The study does not test whether feature importance or capacity competition causes neuron polysemanticity.
The study does not examine polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
It reports SAE reconstruction of activations, but does not test whether features are interpretable or spread across neurons, or compare SAE recovery with other feature dictionaries.
Reconstruction fidelity and its change under continual fine-tuning are measured. Semantic completeness and whether SAE features are canonical or uniquely determined are not tested.
The study uses dictionary feature directions but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.value: 90.29% after task 8; decrease of 4.36 percentage points
rows.note: The authors report a gradual decrease across tasks, while reconstruction remains above 90%.
rows.check: This is a tool-validity check on the frozen Vicuna SAE under domain shift and fine-tuning (Appendix I). Reconstruction fidelity under drift does not measure whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units, and it is not evidence of superposition in the LLM. Values are read correctly: 94.65% falls to 90.29%.

relation.reason: The study uses SAE decomposition and superposition as motivation and tools without independently testing feature overlap, capacity allocation, dictionary completeness or canonicality, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: SAE-FD uses SAE representations for continual-learning regularization. Reconstruction checks and method-performance comparisons do not test any listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The >99% result concerns held-out SAE training-distribution activations; 94.65% is the base-model result on TRACE data. Frozen-SAE reconstruction fidelity does not establish stable or complete semantic features.
